n: The heading links this psalm to Doeg the Edomite, who informed Saul that the priests of Nob had helped David, then killed them. David asks the “mighty man” why he brags about evil, when God’s loyal love outlasts it all.

f.g: Spoken with irony — a so-called hero who is really a villain.

n: His tongue plots destruction and cuts like a razor — slick, sharp and treacherous.
He actually prefers evil to good and lies to truth.

f.w: Thou lovest evil more than good

n: He loves words that devour and destroy others.

f.g: Words that swallow up and ruin people.

n: But God will tear him down permanently — snatch him from his tent and uproot him from life, like a tree pulled up by its roots.

f.g: This life, the world of the living.

n: The righteous will see it with awe and laugh — not cruelly, but at how foolish his boasting turned out to be.
Look at the man who wouldn’t make God his fortress, but trusted in his money and grew strong through wickedness.

f.w: trusted in the abundance of his riches

n: David contrasts himself: the uprooted tree versus a flourishing olive tree planted near God’s house. Olive trees live for centuries and stay green — a picture of lasting life rooted in God’s love.
He will praise God forever for what he has done and hope in his name among the faithful.

f.g: Hebrew ḥasidim — the faithful, loyal ones.
